brief: A system monitor where CPU/memory are organisms — healthy breathes steady, stressed pulses fast

dominant_strengths: Clean dark canvas with confident hierarchy; large percentage figures and section labels read instantly without competing with the orbs.
The breathing-orb metaphor is visually clear; concentric rings around CPU hint at pulse rhythm tied to load state.
Restrained palette (green/blue) maps cleanly to organism identity and keeps the dashboard calm and legible.
dominant_weaknesses: Static screenshot can't convey the core brief — the 'breathing vs pulsing' motion is the entire concept and isn't expressed structurally.
Memory orb shows no concentric pulse rings unlike CPU, breaking visual parity and weakening the organism-system metaphor.
Bottom metrics row is generic dashboard chrome — no organism language, no living indicator, feels bolted on from a different design.
fix_priorities: Unify the two organisms with shared ring/pulse vocabulary, varying only rhythm and amplitude by stress level.
Encode load state into orb deformation, glow intensity, and ring frequency so a still frame still implies motion.
Reframe the bottom stats as smaller satellite organisms or vital signs rather than a flat KPI strip.
Add micro-typographic rhythm cues (e.g., bpm-style labels) tying numbers to the living metaphor.
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral pull from the glowing orbs, weak behavioral expression because the living metaphor depends on motion that isn't shown, and modest reflective payoff once novelty fades.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially fits: the organism visual is established, but without motion differentiation between healthy and stressed, the brief's core idea is only half-delivered.
